cases.name: Lori Hedges Conners
cases.about: Her obituary said, "There are people who cross our paths in this life that have a spirit of compassion so unique and strong that all who interact with them are left with a lasting impression. Lori was one of them. Whether it was sponsoring needy children, feeding and helping locals in need, doting on her grandchildren (and of course, letting them win all the card games), dropping everything to help her children any way she could, or simply smiling at someone who needed it, Lori wanted to make sure anyone with a need had them met. While she had many admirable qualities, this was certainly one that separated her from the crowd, and the world has a little more love in it thanks to her. Lori was a woman with a variety of interests and talents. An avid gardener, she transformed more than one home from typical to remarkable with her keen eye and vast knowledge of all things botanical. Her creative pursuits extended inside the house as well-all who were fortunate enough to see her house (especially during the holidays!) can attest to this. She was also interested in architecture and history and was so grateful she was able to see so much of both on her trip to Ireland and her Mediterranean cruise. Her favorite pastime of all, though, was spending time with her children and grandchildren; nothing brought a smile to her face like they did.
cases.narrative: He claimed her death was the result of assisted suicide because she was suffering from cancer and he held the gun to her head and she pulled the trigger.
